Job Title: PCU Registered Nurse (Night Shift)

Job Location:8700 Beverly Blvd West Hollywood, CA 90048
Working Hours: Night 4x12-Hour (19:00 – 07:30) | 36 or 48 Hours Available
Department: Progressive Care Unit (PCU)
Assignment Duration: 13–15 Weeks

Position Summary:

The Progressive Care Unit (PCU) Registered Nurse plays a vital role in delivering specialized care to complex post-operative and telemetry patients, including fresh post-op kidney transplant cases. This position requires strong clinical judgment, critical thinking, and the ability to provide advanced monitoring and interventions in a fast-paced, high-acuity environment. The ideal candidate demonstrates professional integrity, adaptability, and a patient-centered approach aligned with Cedars-Sinai’s standards of excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

• Deliver compassionate, high-quality patient care to moderate-to-high acuity PCU patients.
• Monitor and manage patients requiring invasive hemodynamic devices and frequent assessments (every 2 hours).
• Administer and titrate vasoactive drips, including Milrinone, Dopamine, and Dobutamine.
• Care for patients with TR Bands, chest tubes, and pulmonary hypertension therapy.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to ensure safe and coordinated patient transitions.
• Complete thorough documentation and uphold HIPAA compliance and patient confidentiality.
• Participate in patient and family education, ensuring clear communication and comfort during care.
• Maintain unit cleanliness and follow safety protocols for infection prevention and equipment use.
• Successfully complete the EKG competency exam on the first day of orientation (required to continue contract).

Required Qualifications & Skills:

• Minimum 2 years of PCU experience (strongly preferred).
• First-time travelers accepted with at least 3 years of experience.
• Proficient in telemetry interpretation, IV starts, and acute patient management.
• Strong organizational, multitasking, and communication skills.
• Ability to adapt quickly and perform in high-acuity settings.

Required Certifications:

• ACLS – Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support
• BLS – Basic Life Support

Preferred Certifications:

• NIH Stroke Scale Certification

Core Competencies:

• Deliver patient-focused, compassionate care with professionalism and empathy.
• Demonstrate advanced clinical skills and judgment in monitoring and intervention.
• Collaborate effectively with physicians, nurses, and interdisciplinary care teams.
• Maintain accuracy in assessments, documentation, and compliance with standards.
• Stay adaptable and proactive in fast-paced, critical care environments.

Additional Information:

• Contract Duration: 13–15 Weeks
• RTO Policy: No RTO within the first 2 weeks of the assignment. Must work 3 of 5 major holidays (Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve/Day, New Year’s Eve/Day).
• Flu Vaccination: Required when flu season begins.
• Unit Type: True PCU – managing complex, high-acuity patients.
• Special Equipment: Swan-Ganz, Transvenous Pacer.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome and valued.
We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, identities, abilities, and experiences. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

Job Title: Registered Nurse – Labor & Delivery
Job Location: Oklahoma City, OK
Working Hours: 12*3
Department: Labor & Delivery
 
Position Summary
Under general supervision, the Registered Nurse – Labor & Delivery provides comprehensive nursing care to patients in all stages of pregnancy, labor, delivery, and postpartum recovery. The role involves delivering safe, compassionate, and evidence-based care to both mother and newborn, while collaborating closely with the interdisciplinary healthcare team to ensure optimal outcomes for families.
Key Responsibilities
  • Provide skilled nursing care to patients in the Labor & Delivery unit, assuming responsibility for an assigned group of patients.
  • Document patient responses to nursing interventions and prescribed treatments; update and record any changes in physician orders.
  • Assist physicians during labor, delivery, and minor procedures; monitor maternal and fetal well-being throughout labor and delivery.
  • Obtain and monitor physiological data; identify abnormal findings and intervene appropriately.
  • Administer medications, initiate and regulate IV infusions, and manage blood product administration as prescribed.
  • Support and educate patients and families on birth plans, hospital procedures, and postnatal care.
  • Collaborate effectively with physicians, midwives, and support staff to ensure a smooth workflow and high-quality patient outcomes.
  • Delegate appropriate tasks to support staff and ensure care continuity.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.
 
Required Qualifications & Skills
  • Knowledge of professional nursing theory, principles, and evidence-based practices related to Labor & Delivery.
  • Ability to organize, plan, coordinate, and evaluate nursing care services.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills to collaborate effectively with team members and patients’ families.
  • Ability to provide culturally competent care and address diverse patient needs.
  • Basic computer proficiency for electronic documentation and patient charting.
 
Certifications & Licensure:
  • Current RN License issued by the Oklahoma State Board of Nursing or a valid multistate compact RN License (eNLC).
  • Basic Life Support (BLS) – American Heart Association.
  • Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) – American Heart Association.
  • Intermediate Fetal Monitoring certification.
  • Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) – Advanced Provider or Instructor certification.
 
Core Competencies
  • Expertise in Labor, Delivery, and Postpartum Care
  • Clinical Assessment & Critical Thinking
  • Patient Advocacy & Family Support
  • Effective Communication & Collaboration
  • Emergency Response & Crisis Management
  • Compassionate and Culturally Sensitive Care
  • Professionalism & Accountability

  • 3+ years coding auditing/education experience strongly preferred.
  • Certification required: RHIA, RHIT, CCS, or CPC.
  • Expert knowledge of ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT-4, MS-DRGs, POA, and APCs.
  • Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Proficiency in Trauma Coding.
